professionalSummary: Experienced frontend engineer with a proven track record in developing and maintaining alert queue and case views for compliance applications using TypeScript and Angular. Demonstrated ability to own comprehensive test suites, reduce load times dramatically, coordinate API changes, and document release details.
experienceHighlights: Developed and maintained alert queue and case views, implementing server‑side paging and column virtualization to replace full‑queue downloads.
Owned component (Jest) and end‑to‑end (Cypress) test suites, ensuring continuous pipeline success and adding a queue‑load smoke test.
Reduced median alert‑queue load time from 6.2 s to 1.4 s, meeting the published performance baseline.
Coordinated API changes with backend team, adapting views to new paged endpoints.
Authored release notes detailing known limitations and hand‑over conditions for frontend on‑call.
projectsAndWorkSamples: Real‑user monitoring export showing median queue load time over eight weeks with baseline and release marker; Cypress smoke test with pipeline run identifiers as verification trail.
optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The provided resume and work samples establish the candidate’s direct experience with alert queue and case view development, test suite ownership, load‑time improvement, API coordination, and release documentation. They do not provide evidence of broader product ownership, cross‑team leadership, or experience beyond the described project.

decisionBoundary.statement: Candidate meets all listed requirements based on provided evidence; human review recommended to confirm fit.

evidence.text: Developed and maintained the alert queue and case views of the compliance web application (TypeScript, Angular), including the server-side paging and column virtualisation that replaced the full-queue download.

Work sample: the real-user monitoring export (median queue load time per day for eight weeks, baseline line, paging release marker) and the Cypress smoke test, with the pipeline run identifiers as a verification trail.
Owned the component test suite (Jest) and the end-to-end suite (Cypress) for the application, keeping both passing in the pipeline and adding a queue-load smoke test that gates releases.

Median alert-queue load time for analysts fell from 6.2 seconds to 1.4 seconds after the paging release, measured by the application's real-user monitoring over the following four weeks against the published baseline of 6.2 seconds.
Coordinated API changes with the backend team in the API review; the backend lead approved endpoint changes and I adapted the views to the paged endpoints.

Wrote the release notes for each application release, including the known limitation that column sorting was applied per page rather than across the whole queue, and the hand-over notes for the frontend on-call.
